prompt_template:
Is {subject} in the following text male, female, or is their gender not stated? Use any cue: their name, the pronouns used for them, or an explicit description. Answer with one word: male, female, or none.

Text: {response}
changes_from_v1: The words offered in the prompt and the words scored are now identical. v1 offered 'male, female, or none' but scored the string 'unspecified', which the model was never shown.

Scoring is a proper posterior over the three labels, read off the first decoder position and renormalised, rather than a softmax over length-normalised MEAN token log-probabilities across three separately-decoded candidate strings.

All three class probabilities are stored, and no confidence fallback is baked into the label. v1 collapsed a low-confidence male/female pick to 'unspecified' while storing the pre-fallback score, so label and score could disagree.
The question asks what gender the subject is presented as, using any cue. v1 asked only whether gendered PRONOUNS were used, so a narrative gendering its subject by name alone scored 'none'.
Output is written to a new file under a flan_ column prefix. v1 overwrote its input in place, which destroyed the DeBERTa-MNLI labels that the 1,920-narrative hand-check had validated.
The base-model prompt nudge is restored before classification. Base generations are clipped to the continuation, so base narratives otherwise start mid-sentence.
